Experience providing consultation and recommendations on complex infection prevention matters

The Ambulatory Infection Prevention Coordinator 4 provides advanced infection prevention expertise across outpatient clinics, procedural areas, and specialty services. The position independently conducts risk-based assessments, evaluates clinical practices, investigates complex infection prevention concerns, and provides recommendations based on current standards, regulatory requirements, and best practices. Responsibilities include evaluating infection prevention practices related to patient care, clinical procedures, cleaning, disinfection and sterilization, medical equipment, and the care environment. The position provides consultation on infection prevention considerations associated with new and expanding clinical services, equipment and technologies, construction, renovation, and environmental conditions. Responsibilities also include surveillance and evaluation of infection trends, patient/employee exposure and transmission investigations, response to communicable diseases and emerging infectious threats, and support for regulatory and accreditation readiness. The position reviews and interprets data, evaluates the effectiveness of infection prevention measures, and serves as a subject matter expert on complex infection prevention matters. Also contributes to the review of policies and development of educational resources.

Ambulatory Infection Prevention Assessments and Oversight – 30% Independently conducts risk-based infection prevention assessments across ambulatory clinics, procedural areas, and specialty services. Evaluates clinical practices, workflows, equipment, and care environments for alignment with infection prevention standards and regulatory requirements. Identifies infection prevention risks, provides recommendations, and assesses the effectiveness of infection prevention practices. Conducts assessments of new and existing ambulatory services as appropriate.

Advanced Infection Prevention Consultation and Risk Evaluation – 20% Provides expert consultation on infection prevention practices across ambulatory settings, including standard and transmission-based precautions, aseptic technique, environmental cleaning and disinfection, and medical equipment reprocessing. Evaluates infection prevention considerations related to clinical services, procedures, equipment, and technologies. Assesses infection prevention risks associated with construction, renovation, water systems, and environmental conditions and provides recommendations based on applicable standards and guidelines.

Exposure Investigations and Communicable Disease Response – 15% Independently assesses and investigates potential exposures, communicable disease concerns, suspected transmission events, and breaches in infection prevention practices. Evaluates infection prevention risks, provides recommendations for appropriate precautions and follow-up, and completes required documentation, notifications, and reporting in accordance with applicable policies and regulatory requirements.

Regulatory Compliance, Standards, and Survey Readiness – 15% Interprets and applies federal and state regulatory requirements, accreditation standards, professional guidelines, and manufacturer instructions for use. Evaluates infection prevention practices for compliance with applicable requirements and provides recommendations to support regulatory and accreditation readiness. Reviews policies and procedures for alignment with current infection prevention standards and provides guidance on their application across ambulatory settings.

Clinical Service Assessments and Quality Improvement – 10% Conducts infection prevention assessments related to new clinics, expanding services, and changes in clinical practices. Evaluates infection prevention considerations associated with new procedures, equipment, and clinical workflows. Reviews assessment findings and relevant data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement. Develops recommendations and evaluates the effectiveness of infection prevention practices and interventions.

Education and Technical Consultation – 10% Develops and provides infection prevention education, training, and resources relevant to ambulatory care. Serves as a subject matter expert on infection prevention standards and clinical practices. Provides guidance on complex infection prevention questions and supports the consistent application of evidence-based practices across ambulatory settings.
Total Effort: 100%
